logicVersionContext: Logic Pro for Mac 12.3 selected in Apple's live guide at retrieval

source.identity: Apple, Logic Pro Effects for Mac

entries.name: Amp Designer
entries.documentedMechanism: Recombinable amp, cabinet, EQ, microphone, position/distance, gain-stage, reverb, tremolo, and vibrato model.
entries.productionConsequence: Gain, Master, and Output are distinct; EQ can change drive, and cabinet/microphone choices change tone and phase. Exact analog behavior remains undocumented.

entries.name: Bass Amp Designer
entries.documentedMechanism: Parallel modeled bass-amp and six-curve DI paths with selectable cabinet/direct tap points, microphones, compressor, and reorderable additional EQ.
entries.productionConsequence: Blend and routing can preserve a clean fundamental beside a colored amp path, but alignment, AutoGain bias, low-end phase, and headroom require listening and measurement.

entries.name: Delay Designer
entries.documentedMechanism: A multi-tap delay with up to 26 independently timed, filtered, pitched, panned/spread, and leveled taps; one tap can feed back. Tap high/low cut ordering can create either a passed band or a rejected band.
entries.productionConsequence: It can build rhythmic patterns, diffusion-like clusters, stereo motion, or pitched echoes. Tap density, feedback, and spectral accumulation can mask attacks and words. A visually complex pattern is not automatically musically useful.

entries.name: Echo
entries.documentedMechanism: One tempo-related delay with feedback, spectral Color, and dry/wet balance.
entries.productionConsequence: Appropriate when a simple repeat is clearer than a designed multi-tap field. Repeat timing and color must fit the phrase; feedback can turn a small cue into masking.

entries.name: Sample Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: Delays channels by a number of samples or milliseconds.
entries.productionConsequence: Primarily an alignment and deliberate interchannel-offset tool. It can improve multi-mic summation or create width, but the same offset can cause comb filtering and mono loss. Polarity inversion and delay are different operations.

entries.name: Stereo Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: Independent left/right delays with selectable input source, crossfeed, phase controls, filters, feedback, and routing modes.
entries.productionConsequence: Can create stable stereo echoes or cross-channel motion. Crossfeed and phase choices can build cancellation or runaway density; check both stereo and mono.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 Stereo Delay evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers sample-exact header bypass; one 120 BPM synchronized quarter-note left and eighth-note right state; one free-time 500 ms left and 250 ms right wet-only feedback-zero state; one 35 percent feedback state; Straight routing with exact right-channel silence for a left-only source; one 50 percent left-to-right crossfeed state; first-transition versus settled behavior; decoded-PCM repeatability; exact controlled crossfeed-state save/reload recovery; and one deterministic guitar-like fixture. The measured timing peaks were exactly 500 ms left and 250 ms right in the controlled free-time state. No participant listening, alternate routing menu, right-to-left crossfeed, nonzero deviation, filter sweep, phase matrix, stereo-link profile, sample-rate grid, automation, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: Tape Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: A delay with tempo/free timing, deviation and smoothing, feedback filtering, clipping threshold, clean/diffuse head choices, LFO/flutter, spread, freeze, and dry/wet control.
entries.productionConsequence: Time instability, bandwidth loss, saturation, and feedback filtering can make repeats feel less literal. Those dimensions are separate: “tape” is not one tone. Freeze and high feedback require output and transition safety checks.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 Tape Delay evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers sample-exact header bypass; one exact displayed 120 BPM synchronized default state; one free-time 500 ms wet-only Clean feedback-zero state; one 50 percent feedback state; one Diffuse feedback-zero state; an exact settled Clean peak at 500 ms; directly observed Clean-versus-Diffuse onset, peak, duration, and level differences; first-transition versus settled behavior; decoded-PCM repeatability; exact controlled Diffuse-state save/reload recovery; and one deterministic guitar-like fixture. No participant listening, threshold transfer, filter or modulation grid, feedback extreme, Freeze, spread or stereo matrix, alternate sample-rate profile, automation, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: Bitcrusher
entries.documentedMechanism: Separates amplitude quantization, effective sample-rate division, input drive, thresholded Fold/Clip/Wrap behavior, and dry/effect mixing.
entries.productionConsequence: Downsampling intentionally aliases without changing pitch or speed; bit reduction is not inherently warm and downsampling is not merely dark. Exact nonlinear equations remain undocumented.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Partial direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 evidence at 48 kHz mono: the observed Default Preset was Clip, +3 dB Drive, 8-bit Resolution, 1x Downsampling, 100% Mix, and 0 dB Clip Level. Three settled bypass renders matched the fixture PCM exactly; three settled active renders plus one post-reload render shared one PCM hash. First-transition renders differed briefly, so settled repeats are required. Fold, Wrap, parameter grids, downsampling above 1x, stereo, other rates, musical preference, and Apple's exact implementation remain unmeasured. Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 evidence at 48 kHz mono-to-stereo extends the preserved July 18 Bitcrusher default run without rewriting it. Header bypass was sample-exact to both output channels. Fold, Clip, and Wrap at +3 dB, 8 bit, 1x, 100 percent Mix, and 0 dB Clip Level were each decoded-PCM exact across three renders and pairwise distinct. A one-factor Clip grid directly covered Drive 0, 3, and 11.5 dB; Resolution 4, 8, and 24 bit; Downsampling 1x, 4x, and 16x; Mix 50.40 and 100 percent; and Clip Level -6 and 0 dB. One Wrap state restored exactly after normal save/reload and rendered a deterministic guitar-range fixture identically three times. Harmonic, IMD, alias-spectrum, other-rate, true-stereo, automation, exhaustive-interaction, and human-listening claims remain open. This grants no Logic control authority.

entries.name: ChromaGlow
entries.documentedMechanism: A family of saturation models and style variants with drive, output/mix, a frequency-domain Bypass Below control, and pre/post low/high filtering.
entries.productionConsequence: Model adjectives are product descriptions, not perceptual proof. Bypass Below can leave low-frequency material outside the nonlinear path; it is not a level threshold. Filtering changes what drives the nonlinearity versus what remains afterward. Exact curves and oversampling are undocumented.

entries.name: Clip Distortion
entries.documentedMechanism: Input gain, drive, pre-distortion high-pass, nonlinear clipping, post-distortion low-pass, dry/effect mixing, a final low-pass, shelf shaping, and output control.
entries.productionConsequence: Pre-filtering changes which bands create harmonics; post-filtering removes generated energy. It is therefore not equivalent to clipping followed by one tone knob.

entries.name: Distortion
entries.documentedMechanism: A bipolar-transistor-described distortion with Drive, Tone/high cut, and output compensation.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful as a bounded harmonic-density candidate, but “bipolar” does not establish the exact circuit or transfer curve. Preserve attack, low end, and level explicitly.

entries.name: Distortion II
entries.documentedMechanism: Four documented circuit styles—Growl, Bity, Nasty, and Class AB soft/hard—with pre-gain, drive, tone, and mix controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Different styles should be treated as competing nonlinear hypotheses, not strengths of one algorithm. Class AB modes may add crossover-like character; exact implementation requires measurement.

entries.name: Overdrive
entries.documentedMechanism: A FET-described overdrive with Drive, Tone, and output level.
entries.productionConsequence: Apple's device-family description is not an acoustic guarantee. Compare against other nonlinear options at matched loudness and inspect intermodulation, noise, and transient loss.

entries.name: Phase Distortion
entries.documentedMechanism: A short delay whose modulation comes from a low-pass-filtered version of the input, with intensity, phase-reversal, and mix controls.
entries.productionConsequence: This is input-dependent delay modulation, not ordinary static waveshaping. Its motion follows source content, so percussive and sustained sources behave differently.

entries.name: Adaptive Limiter
entries.documentedMechanism: Look-ahead peak limiting with input gain, output ceiling, an Optimal mode, DC removal, and true-peak detection.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for bounded peak control, not proof of mastering quality. Gain into the limiter changes density and distortion; ceiling alone does not set loudness.

entries.name: Compressor
entries.documentedMechanism: Seven circuit models plus threshold, ratio, knee, attack/release, detector, channel linking, side-chain filter, make-up, parallel mix, output limiter, and distortion.
entries.productionConsequence: “Compression” is a family of envelope decisions. Strategy must state whether it preserves transients, increases density, controls peaks, changes sustain, or reacts to a filtered side chain.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Partial direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 evidence at 48 kHz mono: the exact observed Compressor Default Preset produced level-dependent gain with Auto Gain -12 dB active and repeated with identical decoded PCM three times. Header bypass matched the source PCM exactly in three renders. In a controlled Platinum Digital state (threshold -20 dB, ratio 4.1:1, hard knee, Peak detector, 0 ms attack, 51 ms release, Auto Gain/Auto Release/distortion/limiter/side-chain filter off, 100% wet), steady ladder reduction matched the exposed hard-knee ratio relation within 0.000128 dB at the five above-threshold steps. The first controlled render differed from stabilized renders only in samples 1...1022; controlled render 2, render 3, and two post-reload renders were decoded-PCM identical. Logic restored the displayed controlled state after project reopen. This does not characterize time behavior, seven models, stereo linking, side-chain filters, distortion, limiter, parallel mix, sample-rate dependence, or musical preference. Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 Compressor evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 extends the frozen controlled Platinum curve. Continuous 1 kHz steps separated attack 0/50 ms and release 51/490 ms; matched controls distinguished Platinum and Vintage VCA/FET/Opto. All admitted state pairs were PCM-identical after transition exclusion. Left-only Max versus Sum differed by 4.54587 dB; an asymmetric probe showed the same linked gain on the low-level opposite channel. Vintage Opto displayed state and PCM survived reload exactly. Header bypass matched the source on both output channels, and settled re-enable restored exact pre-bypass PCM. Other circuits, RMS, auto gain/release, side-chain filters/external side chain, distortion, limiter, mix, grids, rates, automation, latency/tail, listening, private topology, and TrackSmith Logic authority remain unproven or prohibited.

entries.name: DeEsser 2
entries.documentedMechanism: Relative or absolute detection, selectable frequency/range, split-band or wideband attenuation, and bounded maximum reduction.
entries.productionConsequence: Sibilance is event- and phoneme-dependent. High-frequency energy supports a hypothesis but is not a diagnosis; preserve intelligibility and breath.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 DeEsser 2 evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers Relative/Absolute level dependence, Split/Wide range behavior, Band Stop/Shelving at 7001 Hz, 20 and 6 dB maximum-reduction states, short/static 7 kHz events, mono/stereo channel behavior, repeatability, source-exact bypass, restoration, and save/reload. Relative reduced quiet/loud same-ratio pairs equally; Absolute did not. Split left 500 Hz effectively unchanged while Wide reduced 500 Hz and 7 kHz together. A 6 dB maximum state bounded measured 7 kHz reduction at 6 dB. Accepted settled pairs were PCM-identical after explicitly retained first-transition exclusions. No human listening, phoneme claim, alternate frequency/sample-rate grid, automation, dedicated latency/tail profile, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: Enveloper
entries.documentedMechanism: Independently changes attack and release portions using detector and gain stages.
entries.productionConsequence: A direct candidate for snap, softness, sustain, or room emphasis. Increasing release also raises spill/noise/ambience; transient enhancement can worsen cymbals.

entries.name: Expander
entries.documentedMechanism: Upward expansion above a threshold with ratio, attack/release, knee, lookahead, and gain controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Can increase dynamic contrast and attack, but may exaggerate noise, breaths, bleed, and inconsistent performance. It is not a noise gate.

entries.name: Limiter
entries.documentedMechanism: Peak limiting with lookahead, release, gain/ceiling, legacy/precision behavior, and true-peak option.
entries.productionConsequence: A safety and density tool whose artifacts depend on release, spectral content, and amount of gain reduction. True-peak mode is not a universal delivery guarantee.

entries.name: Multipressor
entries.documentedMechanism: Four crossover bands, each with compression and downward-expansion behavior, plus per-band solo/bypass/gain and overall lookahead/output controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Band-specific dynamics can solve localized instability but crossovers and independent envelopes can change tone, phase, punch, and stereo image. Prefer simpler processing when evidence does not justify four bands.

entries.name: Noise Gate
entries.documentedMechanism: Gate or ducker behavior with threshold, hysteresis, reduction, attack/hold/release, lookahead, and side-chain filtering.
entries.productionConsequence: Hysteresis and hold reduce chatter; aggressive gating can truncate breaths, decays, and room. Ducker mode and gate mode solve different routing problems.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 Noise Gate evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers sample-exact header bypass; one default and one controlled Gate state; one controlled Ducker state; threshold, depth, hysteresis, and two attack/hold/release states at zero lookahead; one 240 Hz to 6900 Hz internal-detector bandpass state; first-transition versus settled behavior; decoded-PCM repeatability; exact controlled-state save/reload recovery; and one deterministic vocal-like fixture. The default -50 dB Gate strongly suppressed the analyzed -60 dBFS steady segment while -48 dBFS and higher segments passed at unity. Transition-sensitive variants produced a distinct first render followed by exact settled repeats. No participant listening, real-source decay-preservation result, external sidechain, lookahead above zero, mono/stereo detector matrix, sample-rate grid, automation, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: Surround Compressor
entries.documentedMechanism: Multichannel compression with group assignments, per-group controls, peak/RMS detection choices, and LFE handling.
entries.productionConsequence: Channel grouping determines image stability. Independent channel compression can move the scene; linked processing can overreact to one channel. TrackSmith cannot infer an immersive strategy from a stereo capture.

entries.name: Channel EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Eight bands with high/low pass, shelves and bells, spectrum analysis, output gain, oversampling, and stereo/L/R/Mid/Side modes.
entries.productionConsequence: General corrective and shaping tool. Analyzer peaks are evidence, not automatic cut targets. Mid/Side edits require mono and center/side preservation checks.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Partial direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 evidence at 48 kHz mono: Channel EQ's settled unmodified Default Preset and settled header-bypass path were sample-transparent for the 1 kHz amplitude ladder. A Peak 3 state of 1000 Hz, +6.0 dB, Q 1.00 produced approximately +6 dB at input peaks from -60 through -12 dBFS, reached full scale at -6 dBFS, clipped louder steps, repeated with identical decoded PCM three times, and survived save/reload with identical PCM. First renders after default insertion and bypass differed only in samples 1...1023, so settling repeats remain mandatory. Other bands, filter slopes, Q/frequency grids, HQ, channel modes, phase/group delay, analyzer switching, automation, stereo, other rates, and musical preference remain unmeasured. Bounded direct Logic Pro 12.3 build-6674 Channel EQ evidence on generated PCM24 fixtures at 48 and 96 kHz. At 48 kHz, settled neutral and header-bypass sweep renders reproduced the mono source PCM exactly on both interleaved output channels. Artifact-backed impulse states cover a 1 kHz +6 dB/Q1 bell, a 2.5 kHz -6 dB/Q4 bell, paired shelves, paired 24 dB/octave cuts, and one eight-band multiband shape. The exposed HQ mode measurably changed that shape; Analyzer POST/OFF/PRE and Q-Couple on/off-with-rewritten-Q comparisons nulled in their recorded states; +3 dB output measured 2.999999876 dB. Stereo, Left Only, Right Only, Mid Only, and Side Only were rendered on generated one-sided, in-phase, and anti-phase fixtures. The complex displayed state survived reload, but accepted pre/post reload groups differed by a minute -113.14 dBFS residual, so exact reload PCM is not claimed. A repeated 96 kHz complex-state render was PCM-exact and showed bounded rate-dependent response differences. Automation, exhaustive parameter grids, other channel formats/rates, musical preference, private topology, and any TrackSmith authority to control Logic remain unmeasured or prohibited.

entries.name: Linear Phase EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Similar band architecture while preserving phase relationships at the cost of latency and possible pre-ringing/transient effects.
entries.productionConsequence: Appropriate when phase response is the primary constraint, not automatically “better.” Steep/narrow moves can audibly change onset behavior.

entries.name: Match EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Learns source and reference spectra, computes a difference curve, and permits smoothing, strength, and range control.
entries.productionConsequence: It matches an averaged spectral relation, not performance, dynamics, depth, arrangement, or identity. The reference must be context-compatible and the result listened to at matched level.

entries.name: Single Band EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: One selectable low/high cut, shelf, or parametric band.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for simple bounded moves and automation. A single band can be more defensible than a complex curve when the evidence is local.

entries.name: Vintage Console EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: A modeled console-style EQ with drive/output behavior and band controls.
entries.productionConsequence: The model can couple tone and nonlinearity; control labels do not reveal exact analog transfer behavior. Treat “vintage” as a family of hypotheses.

entries.name: Vintage Graphic EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Multiple fixed-frequency bands with modeled drive/output behavior.
entries.productionConsequence: Fast broad contouring, but adjacent bands interact and fixed centers may not match a measured issue.

entries.name: Vintage Tube EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: A modeled passive/tube-associated equalizer with linked boost/attenuation-style controls and output drive.
entries.productionConsequence: Simultaneous boost/cut interactions can create shapes unlike one bell. Use for a chosen contour/color, not because “tube” guarantees warmth.

entries.name: AutoFilter
entries.documentedMechanism: Envelope-followed and/or LFO cutoff modulation, state-variable and four-pole low-pass modes, resonance/self-oscillation, stereo spread, fatness, and distinct pre/post distortion.
entries.productionConsequence: The source envelope becomes control data. Pre-distortion changes the material seen by the filter; post-distortion colors its output. Resonance and self-oscillation demand peak checks.

entries.name: EVOC 20 Filterbank
entries.documentedMechanism: Two parallel 20-band formant-filter banks with crossfade, shifting, modulation, overdrive, and stereo layout.
entries.productionConsequence: Can morph/filter a source without a carrier vocoder. Formant shifts and resonant bands can make dramatic spectral motion, but intelligibility and level can change rapidly.

entries.name: EVOC 20 TrackOscillator
entries.documentedMechanism: Analysis/synthesis filter banks, unvoiced detection, monophonic pitch tracking, FM oscillator options, pitch quantization, and formant stretch/shift.
entries.productionConsequence: A vocoder and tracked-synthesis system, not transparent correction. Tracking is source-dependent; polyphony/noise/transients can invalidate pitch assumptions.

entries.name: Fuzz-Wah
entries.documentedMechanism: Wah, compressor, and fuzz blocks whose serial order can be changed.
entries.productionConsequence: Order is part of the sound: compression before fuzz changes drive consistency; wah before fuzz changes harmonic generation; wah after fuzz filters generated harmonics.

entries.name: Spectral Gate
entries.documentedMechanism: Splits spectral content around a threshold, exposes super/sub-threshold energy and modulation of center/bandwidth.
entries.productionConsequence: Can isolate or transform spectral strata, but Apple's prose does not fully specify the internal algorithm. Do not infer exact FFT/window/phase behavior without measurement.

entries.name: Binaural Post-Processing
entries.documentedMechanism: Converts or conditions binaural material for speaker/headphone presentation using mode-specific crosstalk-related processing.
entries.productionConsequence: Playback format is part of the meaning. A binaural-to-speaker choice can alter timbre and localization; do not promise translation without the target playback condition.

entries.name: Direction Mixer
entries.documentedMechanism: LR or MS direction/width manipulation, with split high/low controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Changes center/lateral balance and apparent direction, not a scalar “quality.” Low-band side energy and mono-sum behavior are preservation constraints.

entries.name: Spatial Audio Monitoring
entries.documentedMechanism: Monitoring-format and profile choices for spatial playback, including head tracking and music/movie modes.
entries.productionConsequence: This is monitoring/rendering context, not permission for TrackSmith to claim immersive source knowledge. Validation must identify monitoring format and profile.

entries.name: Stereo Spread
entries.documentedMechanism: Alternates frequency bands between channels over a chosen range.
entries.productionConsequence: Can create apparent width from spectral redistribution. It may hollow the mono sum or destabilize low frequencies; Apple specifically warns about low-band use.

entries.name: AVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: Basic algorithmic reverb whose Density/Time jointly moves from discernible reflection clusters toward a denser tail, with predelay, reflectivity, size and mix.
entries.productionConsequence: Fast ambience/echo design; the coupled density/time control prevents independent optimization.

entries.name: Bass Amp
entries.documentedMechanism: Nine legacy amp/DI voicings with pre-gain, bass/mid/treble, sweepable mid frequency and output.
entries.productionConsequence: A compatibility color option. Model/genre descriptions are heuristics and the current Bass Amp Designer exposes a more inspectable amp/DI architecture.

entries.name: DeEsser
entries.documentedMechanism: Separate detector and suppressor frequencies, sensitivity/strength, monitoring and smoothing; the manual says the band is isolated/subtracted rather than split through a crossover.
entries.productionConsequence: Can target detection and reduction bands independently. Legacy behavior may be useful for recall; modern DeEsser 2 offers more explicit relative/absolute and split/wide behavior.

entries.name: Denoiser
entries.documentedMechanism: FFT-based attenuation of low-level, lower-complexity bands below a threshold, with reduction/noise-type and frequency/time/transition smoothing.
entries.productionConsequence: Noise reduction can create musical-noise or smearing artifacts. Find a noise-only region, use minimum sufficient reduction, and compare artifacts against the original noise.

entries.name: DJ EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Fixed high/low shelves plus one parametric band with up to deep cut.
entries.productionConsequence: Broad performance/remix contouring, not surgical or source-diagnostic EQ.

entries.name: Ducker
entries.documentedMechanism: Analyzes an existing side-chain recording to lower an output/aux path with amount, threshold, attack, hold, release and lookahead; it is explicitly not live-input ducking.
entries.productionConsequence: A post/broadcast workflow, not a real-time side-chain compressor substitute. The legacy side chain is mixed back after the plug-in, a routing exception that must be understood.

entries.name: Fat EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Five bands with selectable pass/shelf/bell roles and master output.
entries.productionConsequence: A flexible low-complexity curve; filter-role choices and output gain must be stored.

entries.name: GoldVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: Separately controls early reflections and tail, including room geometry, stereo base, delay, spread, high cut, density, diffusion and RT60-oriented time.
entries.productionConsequence: Early/late balance and predelay govern depth/definition. Manual room analogies remain simplified models.

entries.name: Grooveshifter
entries.documentedMechanism: Delays even eighth/sixteenth positions toward a selected swing amount and can accent them, using beat or granular tonal modes.
entries.productionConsequence: Requires source/project tempo alignment; incorrect tempo or material type degrades timing. It changes performed timing, not merely a groove label.

entries.name: Guitar Amp Pro
entries.documentedMechanism: Recombines 11 amp models, 15 cabinets/direct, four EQ types, condenser/dynamic mic choices, two positions, tremolo/vibrato/reverb, Gain/Master and final Output.
entries.productionConsequence: A legacy but deep amp architecture. Master changes modeled character while Output is final level; model adjectives and mic claims remain model-specific.

entries.name: PlatinumVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: Two-band algorithmic reverb with separate early/tail structure, crossover-dependent low-band time/level, high cut, density/diffusion and dry/wet.
entries.productionConsequence: Can keep low-frequency reverberation shorter/quieter than the upper tail, reducing masking; crossover and band timing can also change body.

entries.name: Silver Compressor
entries.documentedMechanism: Simplified threshold/ratio/attack/release compressor with gain-reduction meter.
entries.productionConsequence: Suitable for a bounded legacy dynamics move, but it lacks the detector/topology controls needed for many source-preservation constraints.

entries.name: Silver EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: High/low shelves plus one parametric band.
entries.productionConsequence: A simple three-band tone tool; limited bands can encourage deliberate broad decisions.

entries.name: Silver Gate
entries.documentedMechanism: Simplified lookahead/threshold/attack/hold/release gate.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for simple cleanup; insufficient context can truncate desired decays and low-level articulation.

entries.name: Single-Band EQs
entries.documentedMechanism: Separate legacy cut/pass/shelf/parametric processors, with filter order/smoothing where exposed.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for exact legacy recall and simple automation; do not assume equivalence to current EQ bands without measurement.

entries.name: Speech Enhancer
entries.documentedMechanism: Combines denoising, built-in-Mac microphone-response models and multiband voice enhancement modes.
entries.productionConsequence: Designed around speech and specific Apple microphones. It must not be treated as a universal vocal-production processor or proof of an “expensive microphone” result.

entries.name: Mastering Assistant
entries.documentedMechanism: Analyzes the project/cycle and offers Clean, Valve, Punch, or Transparent character, Auto EQ, dynamics/excite/width controls, loudness compensation, LUFS/LRA/peak displays, and broad three-band correction.
entries.productionConsequence: It is an interactive starting point, not an oracle. Apple's approximately -14 LUFS-I center is described as typical rather than best or mandatory; platform targets and artistic choices vary. Character words remain product heuristics.

entries.name: BPM Counter
entries.documentedMechanism: Estimated tempo from incoming audio.
entries.productionConsequence: Tempo confidence, meter, groove, subdivisions, or musical correctness for every source.

entries.name: Correlation Meter
entries.documentedMechanism: Time-varying interchannel correlation.
entries.productionConsequence: It cannot establish preferred width, spatial quality, or absence of frequency-local cancellation.

entries.name: Level Meter
entries.documentedMechanism: Peak and RMS-style level with selectable display behavior.
entries.productionConsequence: Standards loudness or perceived quality. Apple's “ears are RMS instruments” wording is pedagogical shorthand, not BS.1770.

entries.name: Loudness Meter
entries.documentedMechanism: Momentary, short-term, integrated loudness, range, target, and start/pause/reset measurement scope.
entries.productionConsequence: It does not establish universal mastering targets or complete formal conformance without external vectors. TrackSmith's own standards algorithms remain independently traceable.

entries.name: MultiMeter
entries.documentedMechanism: Spectrum, goniometer/correlation, peak/RMS/true-peak display, and loudness-oriented views.
entries.productionConsequence: It does not produce a single quality score. Its “AES 128” wording is an apparent manual error; normative claims come from EBU R 128/ITU sources.

entries.name: Surround MultiMeter
entries.documentedMechanism: Multichannel level, correlation, and spectrum-oriented displays.
entries.productionConsequence: An immersive perceptual verdict or unmeasured render/downmix safety.

entries.name: Tuner
entries.documentedMechanism: Fundamental/note tuning feedback for suitable input.
entries.productionConsequence: Reliable pitch for polyphonic, noisy, transient-only, or inharmonic sources.

entries.name: Arpeggiator
entries.documentedMechanism: Orders held notes into patterns with latch, order, octave/inversion, rate, swing, velocity/note-length, live/grid and 16-step controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Converts harmony into a performance pattern. Note order, octave, gate, and swing are musical decisions, not audio-effect parameters.

entries.name: Chord Trigger
entries.documentedMechanism: Maps an input note or note range to learned/transposed chord output.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for repeatable voicings; it can also create collisions, range problems, or unintended harmony.

entries.name: Modifier
entries.documentedMechanism: Transforms selected MIDI event data, including scale/add/reassign-style operations.
entries.productionConsequence: A bounded event mapping tool. It must not be confused with audio modulation or unrestricted scripting.

entries.name: Modulator
entries.documentedMechanism: LFO plus DAHR envelope generation targeting MIDI CC, aftertouch, pitch bend, or an instrument/effect parameter.
entries.productionConsequence: Produces time-varying control. Target range, polarity, tempo relation, and reset behavior must be explicit.

entries.name: Note Repeater
entries.documentedMechanism: Repeats incoming notes with timing and performance controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Creates rolls/retriggers; density and velocity evolution affect groove and instrument voice allocation.

entries.name: Randomizer
entries.documentedMechanism: Randomizes chosen event properties with range/probability and a seed.
entries.productionConsequence: A fixed seed makes repeatable output during bounce; changing the seed is a creative variation, not a deterministic revision unless recorded.

entries.name: Record MIDI to Track Here
entries.documentedMechanism: Captures the MIDI stream after the chosen plug-in-chain location.
entries.productionConsequence: A Logic workflow for committing generated events. It is not ordinary AU host authority available to TrackSmith.

entries.name: Scripter
entries.documentedMechanism: Runs JavaScriptCore-based real-time MIDI scripts using event, timing, parameter, HandleMIDI, and ProcessMIDI APIs; scripts persist with settings/projects.
entries.productionConsequence: Security-critical: untrusted provider text must never become executable Scripter code. TrackSmith has no arbitrary-code authority. Any future scripting feature needs a separate typed DSL, static validation, resource bounds, consent, and host proof.

entries.name: Transposer
entries.documentedMechanism: Constrains/transposes note output by scale and root-related controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for pitch-set mapping, but source harmony and non-note events still need explicit handling.

entries.name: Velocity Processor
entries.documentedMechanism: Shapes, compresses/expands, clips, adds, or randomizes note velocity.
entries.productionConsequence: Changes instrument articulation and sample-layer selection, not merely loudness.

entries.name: Chorus
entries.documentedMechanism: Mixes the source with modulated delayed voice(s).
entries.productionConsequence: Thickens/spreads and can soften pitch definition; check mono and low-frequency use.

entries.name: Ensemble
entries.documentedMechanism: Uses multiple modulated voices for denser chorus-like animation.
entries.productionConsequence: Greater density can sound lush or unfocused; voice count does not prove width or quality.

entries.name: Flanger
entries.documentedMechanism: Modulated short delay with feedback, producing moving comb notches/peaks.
entries.productionConsequence: Can add motion or metallic resonance; feedback and delay center govern severity.

entries.name: Microphaser
entries.documentedMechanism: A simplified phase-sweep effect.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for restrained motion; moving cancellations can alter body and mono translation.

entries.name: Modulation Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: A delay-based chorus/flange architecture with modulation and feedback/routing controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Can range from doubling to obvious flanging; base delay, feedback, and wet relationship are separate dimensions.

entries.name: Phaser
entries.documentedMechanism: Cascaded phase-shift stages under modulation, with feedback and stereo controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Changes frequency-dependent phase/cancellation. Stage count and feedback affect complexity and peaks.

entries.name: Ringshifter
entries.documentedMechanism: Frequency shifting or ring modulation with delay, feedback, envelope/LFO modulation and wet/dry control.
entries.productionConsequence: Frequency shift moves every component by a fixed amount rather than preserving ratios; ring modulation creates sum/difference components. Both can become inharmonic.

entries.name: Rotor Cabinet
entries.documentedMechanism: Rotating-speaker/cabinet simulation with motor speed transitions, cabinet and mic behavior.
entries.productionConsequence: Modulates amplitude, spectrum, phase, and stereo position together. Acceleration/braking is part of phrasing.

entries.name: Scanner Vibrato
entries.documentedMechanism: Scanner-style vibrato/chorus variants.
entries.productionConsequence: Vibrato changes pitch; chorus-style modes combine/directly relate voices. Preserve tuning and mono intent.

entries.name: Spreader
entries.documentedMechanism: Produces stereo spread through frequency- and phase-related processing.
entries.productionConsequence: Apparent width can cost mono solidity. Exact internal response is not fully specified by the prose.

entries.name: Tremolo
entries.documentedMechanism: Tempo/free cyclic amplitude modulation with phase/symmetry/smoothing-related controls.
entries.productionConsequence: A rhythmic level tool, not pitch vibrato. Wave shape, phase and depth can reinforce or fight the groove.

entries.name: Beat Breaker
entries.documentedMechanism: Buffers live input and slices/reorders it with Time, Repeat, Cutoff, Resonance, Volume and Pan modes across ten patterns, per-slice settings, declicking, Bypass Below, and bounded randomization controls.
entries.productionConsequence: A real-time rearrangement effect that leaves the source file unchanged. It can create rhythmic edits, but buffer/slice timing and transient integrity must be auditioned; randomness needs stored state.

entries.name: Phat FX
entries.documentedMechanism: Reorderable serial Bandpass, Filter, three distortion slots, modulation FX, Bass Enhancer and Compressor, driven by two LFOs, an envelope follower and XY controls, with mix/output/limiter.
entries.productionConsequence: The same modules in different orders are different processors. Preset-level adjectives cannot substitute for graph inspection.

entries.name: Remix FX
entries.documentedMechanism: Performance-oriented XY Filter, Wobble, Orbit, Repeater, Reverb and Delay plus Gater, Downsampler, Reverse, Scratch and Tape Stop controls, all usable with automation.
entries.productionConsequence: Best understood as gesture/performance processing. A static setting does not capture the automation trajectory that creates the result.

entries.name: Step FX
entries.documentedMechanism: Reorderable Mod FX, delay, filter, distortion and reverb, driven by three independent up-to-128-step modulators plus envelope, gate/pan, polyrhythm and XY control.
entries.productionConsequence: Enables deterministic rhythmic motion when every pattern/state is stored. Polyrhythmic modulation can create long cycles; transition/reset behavior matters.

entries.name: Pedalboard
entries.documentedMechanism: Left-to-right serial pedal graph with two buses, movable split/recombination points, frequency splitting, panning, channel-format transitions, automation, and eight macros.
entries.productionConsequence: Pedal order and branch topology are part of the sound. Parallel and split-band designs require level, phase, crossover, stereo, and mono checks.

entries.name: Blue Echo
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds tempo-free or tempo-synced repeats; a fixed filter biases repeat spectrum.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Time, Repeats, Mix, Lo/Hi/Off Tone Cut, Mute, Sync. Mute passes dry signal while existing repeats continue. Risks/checks: Feedback density can mask rhythm or words; match level and check repeat timing in context.

entries.name: Spring Box
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds algorithmic spring-style reverberant energy.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Short/medium/long Time, Tone cutoff, Boutique/Simple/Vintage/Bright/Resonant Style, Mix. Risks/checks: Bright/resonant modes can emphasize pick noise or sibilance; long settings can blur articulation.

entries.name: Tie Dye Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: Reverses delayed material, with feedback and spectral shaping.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Time/Sync, Feedback, Tone, fixed Bright/Dark EQ, Mix, Listen tail behavior. Risks/checks: Reverse attacks can pre-echo or obscure the source rhythm; feedback can accumulate.

entries.name: Tru-Tape Delay
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds normal or reverse tape-style repeats with bandwidth limiting, saturation, and time instability.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Lo/Hi Cut, Dirt, Flutter, Time/Sync, Feedback, Mix. Feedback automation can build self-reinforcing dub effects. Risks/checks: Dirt changes both repeat tone and dynamics; high feedback can become unstable/loud; flutter can compromise pitch focus.

entries.name: Candy Fuzz
entries.documentedMechanism: Bright, aggressive fuzz through input drive and output level.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Drive controls how hard the nonlinear stage is hit; Level is not a substitute for Drive. Risks/checks: Added upper harmonics, aliasing/noise, and reduced transient contrast; level-match.

entries.name: Double Dragon
entries.documentedMechanism: Combines saturation, compression, nonlinear contour, tone, parallel blend, and fixed Bright/Fat shelving.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Input and Drive jointly set operating point; Squash changes dynamics; Contour changes distortion; Mix restores dry signal. Risks/checks: Many controls are coupled. A louder/brighter result can masquerade as better; inspect envelope and preserved low end.

entries.name: Fuzz Machine
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds American-style fuzz; Tone simultaneously raises treble and reduces lows.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Fuzz, Level, Tone. Risks/checks: Tone is a tilt-like tradeoff, not independent treble gain; can thin a guitar or expose noise.

entries.name: Grinder
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds driven, filtered, lo-fi metal distortion with optional mid/tonal scoop.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Grind, harshness/crunch Filter, Level, Full/Scoop fixed Gain/Q setting. Risks/checks: Scoop can reduce audibility in a dense mix despite sounding large in solo; high Filter can become painful.

entries.name: Grit
entries.documentedMechanism: Uses separate input and output drive around a harsh/crunch filter.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Volume drives input, Filter changes edge, Distortion drives output. Risks/checks: Two drive locations make gain staging decisive; easily obscures keyboard voicing or guitar articulation.

entries.name: Happy Face Fuzz
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds softer, fuller fuzz with minimal controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Fuzz, Volume. Risks/checks: “Softer” is relative to the family, not transparent; bass buildup and intermodulation still require checking.

entries.name: Hi-Drive
entries.documentedMechanism: Overdrives either a high-frequency portion or the full-range signal.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Treble/Full selects processing range; Level controls output. Risks/checks: Treble mode can intensify hiss, pick edge, cymbals, or sibilance; Full can alter low-end definition.

entries.name: Monster Fuzz
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds high saturation with independently adjustable input gain, saturation, tonal color, texture, grain, and output.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Roar, Growl, Tone, Texture, Grain, Level. Higher Tone also lowers overall volume according to the manual. Risks/checks: Coupled tone/level invites biased comparisons; nonlinear texture can destroy note separation.

entries.name: Octafuzz
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds fat fuzz with integrated high-pass tone shaping.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Fuzz, Level, high-pass Tone cutoff. Risks/checks: Raising cutoff removes fundamental/body while generated harmonics remain; verify intended weight.

entries.name: Rawk! Distortion
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds metal/hard-rock saturation with a brightness control.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Crunch, Level, Tone. Risks/checks: Bright high-gain settings can amplify fizz and fatigue; context and level matching are essential.

entries.name: Tube Burner
entries.documentedMechanism: Combines tube-style drive, crossover-bias control, compression, multi-band tone shaping, and optional bass enhancement.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Fat, Low, Mid Freq/Gain, High, Tone, Bias, Squash, Drive, Output. Risks/checks: Bias can intentionally introduce crossover distortion; Fat and low EQ can overload downstream stages; Squash may erase playing dynamics.

entries.name: Vintage Drive
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds FET-described overdrive with Tone and optional low-frequency enhancement.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Drive, Tone, Fat, Level. Risks/checks: Apple's “warmer than bipolar” description is a model heuristic, not a universal semiconductor law; verify spectrum/envelope.

entries.name: Auto-Funk
entries.documentedMechanism: Moves a band-pass or low-pass filter in response to input level.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Sensitivity threshold, Cutoff, BP/LP, preset resonance Hi/Lo, upward/downward modulation. Risks/checks: Performance level becomes modulation control; inconsistent input dynamics can produce inconsistent tone.

entries.name: Classic Wah
entries.documentedMechanism: Manually sweeps filter cutoff with the pedal.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Footpedal position and bypass. Risks/checks: Narrow resonant sweeps can create large peaks; automation timing is part of the performance.

entries.name: Graphic EQ
entries.documentedMechanism: Applies seven fixed-band boosts/cuts plus output level.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Seven frequency sliders and Level. Risks/checks: Adjacent broad bands interact; boosts change headroom into later drive stages.

entries.name: Modern Wah
entries.documentedMechanism: Sweeps a more aggressive wah response or volume, with adjustable resonance.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Pedal, Q, Wah/Volume Mode. Risks/checks: High Q produces narrow pronounced peaks; Volume mode is amplitude control rather than spectral wah.

entries.name: Squash Compressor
entries.documentedMechanism: Reduces signals above a Sustain/threshold setting, then applies output gain.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Sustain, Level, Fast/Slow Attack source mode. Risks/checks: The manual exposes no ratio/release/meter, so behavior must be auditioned; added sustain can raise noise and reduce transient contrast.

entries.name: Flange Factory
entries.documentedMechanism: Modulates short delay to create moving comb filtering, with waveform, symmetry, curve, feedback, and bandwidth control.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, Resonance, Mix, Wave, Symmetry, Curve, Manual delay, Low/High cutoffs. Risks/checks: Feedback and Manual can become metallic; stereo/mono routing and mono fold-down require checks.

entries.name: Heavenly Chorus
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds modulated voices to thicken and potentially stereo-spread the source.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, fixed Bright EQ, Feedback, Density dry/effect relationship. Risks/checks: Feedback can create intermodulation; chorus can soften pitch center and mono definition.

entries.name: Phase Tripper
entries.documentedMechanism: Sweeps phase-derived notches, with feedback.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, Feedback. Risks/checks: Can hollow out essential bands or disappear/change on mono summing.

entries.name: Phaze 2
entries.documentedMechanism: Combines two independently bounded phasers.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Two Rates, Floor/Ceiling ranges, filter Order, Feedback, Tone; LFO mix and Sync. Risks/checks: Overlapping sweeps can become highly nonstationary; higher even order is heavier, odd order subtler per Apple, but exact response remains undocumented.

entries.name: Retro Chorus
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds a restrained chorus with rate and depth.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth. Risks/checks: Even subtle modulation can compromise mono compatibility or pitch stability on bass.

entries.name: Robo Flanger
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds flanging with feedback and a manual base delay.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, Feedback, Manual. Risks/checks: High feedback plus short delay can create resonant metallic peaks.

entries.name: Roswell Ringer
entries.documentedMechanism: Ring-modulates/frequency-shifts content, creating sum/difference components that can sound metallic, tremolo-like, brighter, or unrecognizable.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Linear/exponential curve, Freq, Fine, Feedback, Mix. Risks/checks: Generally inharmonic sidebands can destroy tonal identity; low frequencies may act more like tremolo.

entries.name: Roto Phase
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds phase movement with a fixed-EQ “Vintage” option.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Intensity, Vintage/Modern. Risks/checks: The style switch includes EQ, so a preference may be tonal rather than modulation-specific.

entries.name: Spin Box
entries.documentedMechanism: Emulates a rotating-speaker cabinet with acceleration/braking, cabinet tone, drive, and horn brightness.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Cabinet, Fast Rate, Response inertia, Drive, Bright, Slow/Brake/Fast. Risks/checks: Movement, distortion, brightness, and stereo behavior are coupled; speed transitions must fit phrasing.

entries.name: The Vibe
entries.documentedMechanism: Provides three vibrato and three chorus variations derived from scanner-vibrato behavior.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, V1-V3/C1-C3 Type. Risks/checks: Vibrato changes pitch; chorus mixes/modifies voices. They should not be treated as interchangeable “movement.”

entries.name: Total Tremolo
entries.documentedMechanism: Modulates amplitude with variable waveform and controllable acceleration.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, Wave, Smooth, Volume, half/double/accelerate/decelerate controls. Risks/checks: Deep or sharp modulation can erase attacks or conflict with groove; post gain can bias audition.

entries.name: Trem-O-Tone
entries.documentedMechanism: Applies simple cyclic amplitude modulation.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Rate/Sync, Depth, Level. Risks/checks: Tremolo is level modulation, not pitch vibrato; verify rhythmic phase and audibility in context.

entries.name: Dr. Octave
entries.documentedMechanism: Adds two octave-shifted voices plus optional output overdrive.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Octave 1/2 levels, Direct balance, Drive. Risks/checks: Tracking/artifact behavior depends on source; added sub-octaves can overload low end and lose definition on chords.

entries.name: Wham
entries.documentedMechanism: Continuously pitch-shifts under pedal control and blends shifted/direct signals.
entries.productionConsequence: Controls/interactions: Pedal position, Tune, Mix. Risks/checks: Formants/timbre, transient smear, polyphonic tracking, and automation gestures require listening; mixed paths can create beating.

entries.name: Mixer
entries.documentedMechanism: Solos A/B or blends them, sets relationship/level, pans each bus, and can change mono/stereo state in mono-to-stereo instances.
entries.productionConsequence: It defines where branches recombine. Moving it changes graph topology; pan and mode can materially affect mono compatibility.

entries.name: Splitter
entries.documentedMechanism: Routes equally to both buses or sends lows to A and highs to B around a chosen frequency.
entries.productionConsequence: Enables parallel and split-band pedal designs; crossover/recombination and branch gain must be checked.

entries.name: Pitch Correction
entries.documentedMechanism: Monophonic pitch correction against a scale/grid with input-range detection, response/tolerance, bypass notes, and reference tuning.
entries.productionConsequence: Best for a single pitched line. Scale choice and response affect musical expression; noisy/polyphonic input and deliberate slides/vibrato can fail.

entries.name: Pitch Shifter
entries.documentedMechanism: Pitch transposition with source-oriented algorithms such as Drums, Speech, Vocals, Manual and Pitch Tracking, plus latency compensation/mix controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Algorithm must fit source. Transposition can alter transients, formants and texture; latency and parallel blending require checks.

entries.name: Vocal Transformer
entries.documentedMechanism: Separates pitch/formant-style controls and adds robotize/grain-related transformation while retaining unvoiced components.
entries.productionConsequence: Creative voice transformation, not transparent identity preservation. Monophonic assumptions and unvoiced handling limit generality.

entries.name: ChromaVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: Algorithmic room models with predelay, attack/early/late relationships, size/density/decay, frequency-dependent damping, modulation, distance, width, low-frequency mono, and output EQ.
entries.productionConsequence: Depth is multivariable: dry/wet, predelay, early energy, tail, spectrum and width all matter. Damping changes the decay process; output EQ changes the returned result.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 ChromaVerb evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers a default Room wet-only state, a controlled Digital wet-only state, exact header bypass, impulse onset/peak/tail identity, in-session repeatability, independent left/right matrix behavior, and save/reload. Room first wet output followed the source impulse by 387 frames at the recorded 8 ms predelay and had a 2.597-second bounded tail. Digital first wet output followed by 1921 frames at the recorded 40 ms predelay and had a 3.642-second bounded tail. Default Room repeated exactly three times; Digital repeated exactly after bounded first-transition exclusion. Digital controls restored visibly across reload and settled within-session, but pre-save and post-reload settled PCM were not exact. No participant listening, other twelve room algorithms, mixed dry/wet state, alternate quality, width, Mono Maker, damping/Output EQ sweep, automation, sample-rate grid, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: EnVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: Shapes the reverb tail with a time envelope rather than only one decay constant.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for gated, reverse-like or contour-specific ambience. Envelope timing must fit the source phrase and can expose abrupt boundaries.

entries.name: Quantec Room Simulator
entries.documentedMechanism: QRS and YardStick algorithm families with separate direct/first-reflection/tail levels, Freeze/Add/Clear behavior, frequency-dependent time controls, and model-specific drive/complexity/density/correlation controls.
entries.productionConsequence: A detailed algorithmic-room design tool. Model heritage and adjectives do not establish physical accuracy; freeze/add states and tail level must be managed explicitly.

entries.name: SilverVerb
entries.documentedMechanism: A compact algorithmic reverb with predelay, reflectivity/room-size/density-time, modulation and wet/dry-oriented controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful when a bounded ambience is sufficient. Fewer controls do not make the outcome source-independent.

entries.name: Space Designer
entries.documentedMechanism: Convolution with recorded or synthesized impulse responses, including IR sample-rate/length/envelope/filter/EQ and stereo/surround handling.
entries.productionConsequence: Captures an IR's linear time-invariant response, not every nonlinear or time-varying property of hardware/space. IR changes may require recalculation and not all parameters are automatable.
entries.empiricalEvidenceSummary: Bounded direct Logic 12.3 build-6674 Space Designer evidence at 48 kHz/PCM24 covers one hash-identified generated mono custom IR loaded into one active stereo True Multi state, exact header bypass, impulse onset/peak/tail identity, non-identical L/R output, exact pre-save and post-reload in-session repeatability, and final package recovery with the IR bundled. Both channels first emitted wet output 128 frames after the source impulse. Three pre-save renders shared one decoded PCM hash; the final two post-reload renders shared another. The final post-reload state was within one integer count of pre-save, but 64 left and 249 right samples differed, so exact cross-reload PCM recovery is not established. No participant listening, factory or Synthesized IR, alternate process mode, parameter grid, stereo matrix, musical-source evidence, sample-rate grid, automation, private topology, musical-superiority claim, or TrackSmith Logic-control authority is established.

entries.name: Exciter
entries.documentedMechanism: High-passes the source for nonlinear harmonic generation, then blends generated content with the original; Color choices alter harmonic/intermodulation behavior.
entries.productionConsequence: Creates upper-band content rather than simply boosting existing highs. It can add apparent detail or worsen sibilance, cymbals and intermodulation; Color 2 is documented as producing more intermodulation.

entries.name: SubBass
entries.documentedMechanism: Derives two narrow source bands and synthesizes sine-based subharmonic content at chosen ratios.
entries.productionConsequence: It is subharmonic synthesis, not ordinary pitch-shifting of the waveform. Stable narrow source bands and suitable monitoring are required; added sub can consume headroom and fail on small speakers.

entries.name: Auto Sampler
entries.documentedMechanism: Sends notes/velocities to a software or external instrument and records key ranges, velocity layers, round robins, sustain/release and optional loop variants into a Sampler instrument. Upstream effects are baked into each sampled note; downstream effects are not.
entries.productionConsequence: Excellent for committing a playable instrument snapshot. Effects become per-note sample character rather than editable time-varying mix processing, and the resulting library requires provenance/storage management. TrackSmith cannot invoke this host workflow through its ordinary AU.

entries.name: Down Mixer
entries.documentedMechanism: Maps a surround master to a chosen destination format with per-destination-channel level controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Useful for a quick alternate-format check, not complete delivery validation. Downmix coefficients, correlation and limiting can change loudness and balance.

entries.name: Gain
entries.documentedMechanism: Applies gain, channel-specific polarity inversion, balance, L/R swap and mono sum, with format-dependent controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Fundamental diagnostic/routing tool. Polarity inversion is not a time delay; mono sum is a direct compatibility check; gain changes downstream nonlinear/dynamic behavior.

entries.name: I/O
entries.documentedMechanism: Routes to/from discrete external hardware, with input/output trims, dry/wet, Stereo or Mid/Side format, latency ping and manual sample offset.
entries.productionConsequence: Makes hardware part of Logic's graph. Round-trip latency, conversion, noise and recall must be recorded; ping accuracy improves when other latent processors are bypassed. TrackSmith has no hardware-routing authority.

entries.name: Multichannel Gain
entries.documentedMechanism: Per-channel gain, mute and polarity inversion plus master gain for surround channels.
entries.productionConsequence: Enables diagnostic and balance work by channel. It does not replace a renderer or perceptual spatial evaluation.

entries.name: Test Oscillator
entries.documentedMechanism: Generates static sine/square/noise/needle signals or linear/log sine sweeps, including aliased/anti-aliased square/needle choices, decorrelated noise and level/dim controls.
entries.productionConsequence: Essential for measurement and troubleshooting. Test signals can be dangerously loud and are not musical evaluation; the positive-only needle is specifically useful for polarity/phase inspection.
